reader.requirement: At 1985, FUNCTION ACOS (argument-1), for a numeric argument in [-1, +1] (a literal, an item of any numeric usage or scale, or an arithmetic expression), must return an approximation of the arccosine in radians that lies in [0, pi].

edition-consulted.switches: the D8 edition window: sig.IntroducedIn (85 for the 1989 Intrinsic Function module rows) against ctx.Edition.DialectLevel; COBOL1502/1503 outside it

construct numeric-function-identifier-operand-2002: at 85 a numeric function written where an identifier stands (DISPLAY/MOVE operand) is refused (COBOL0900), per 1985 IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR4; 2002+ accepts it. Not consulted inside COMPUTE

DialectBehavior.UnphrasedSizeErrorIsFatal: at 85 a COMPUTE with no SIZE ERROR phrase catches every size condition and continues (1985 VI.6.4.2 GR3); 2002+ takes the fatal-EC shape. Statement-level, around the function value, not inside it
num.StandardDecimal (arithmetic mode): the ARITHMETIC clause does not exist at 85, so 85 always takes the native arms, the same arms the latest edition takes by default

reader.edition-search: grep of IntrinsicRenderer.cs and the runtime CobolIntrinsics.*.cs for Edition|DialectLevel|CobolVersion|ConstructRegistry|DialectBehavior: the renderer's function dispatch and every runtime body consult no edition (the runtime Intrinsics folder has none); the generated C# at --std 85 and --std 2023 differs only in the assembly Edition attribute and the COMPUTE size-error wrapper (diff of var85-002/var85.g.cs vs var85-003, trig85-001 vs trig85-002)
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the same emitted call (Acos(DomainDecAdmitted(...))) at 85 and 2023; the out-of-domain screen applies the 2023 EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION default at every edition, which at 85 lies within an undefined result
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers ill-conditioned arguments near +-1 only; the bounds -1, 0 and +1, scaled and expression arguments and the range bound are not exercised

probes.printed: ACOS(-1) NOT ABOVE PI (IF ACOS(M1) > 3.14159265358979324); ACOS(1) NOT BELOW ZERO; ACOS(-1) ROUNDED into S9V9(17) = +3.14159265358979300
COBOL1504 ACOS takes 1 argument; COBOL1627 class alphanumeric; ACOS(T(ALL)) COBOL1645; ACOS(2) prints 0 at run time and the program continues
probes.expected: refused; refused; refused (no repeated argument); an out-of-range argument has an undefined result (A.1.2.2), so any value is acceptable

probes.printed: COBOL0900: a numeric or integer function-identifier where an identifier is written requires COBOL-2002 (DISPLAY FUNCTION ACOS(0))

reader.notes: Past |x| = 0.5 the exact-argument body uses the half-angle identity over the exact 1-|x|, and a negative x returns (PiHi - r) + PiLo, which narrows to binary64 pi, below the true pi, so the upper bound holds; ACOS(1) is +0.

refuter.evidence: trigx-001 at --std 85: ACOS(SV9(18) -.999999999999999999)=3.1415926521755795 and ACOS(.999999999999999999)=0.0000000014142135 (pi - sqrt(2E-18), sqrt(2E-18): 18-digit arguments keep their precision); SIGN LEADING SEPARATE -1 and COMP-3 -1 give 3.1415926535897930 (binary64 pi, below true pi); scaled SVPP9 .005 gives 1.5657963059613290; ACOS(FUNCTION ASIN(1) - 1)=0.9633209590730629; ACOS(0) into S9V9(4) truncates 1.5707, ROUNDED 1.5708. Every value lies in [0, pi]. rndmode-001: ROUNDED MODE refused at 85 (COBOL0803). lit19-001: 19-digit literal argument refused (COBOL0802). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.5.4 RV1 ('greater than or equal to zero and less than or equal to pi').
